info.name: MyOperator API Document
info.description:
MyOperator offers an HTTP-based API that follows REST principles, allowing easy integration with standard HTTP clients like cURL. The API URLs are structured around resources, with requests formatted in form-encoded style and responses delivered in JSON.

The API uses two HTTP methods based on the operation type:

  • GET: For read-only operations, such as retrieving a single resource or listing multiple resources.
  • POST: For write operations that modify the state of a resource.

Request

The HTTP method (such as GET or POST) defines the type of operation performed on a resource. For GET requests, query parameters can be used to specify additional options. For POST requests, parameters supply the data needed for write operations, such as creating or updating resources.

Response

The response is in JSON format. Currently, MyOperator does not support any other response format.

Concepts

As you explore the MyOperator WhatsApp API and its documentation, you'll encounter various concepts, variables, and terms essential to understanding its functionality. Below is a guide to these key concepts and where you can locate them within the MyOperator app.

Base URL: The base URL is to access the public APIs. You can use https://publicapi.myoperator.co to access the public APIs

Api Key: MyOperator authenticates your API requests using your account's API keys. You can find the keys on Myoperator Panel > Manage > Whatsapp APIs> Whats app API Key

Company id: A unique identifier of company in MyOperator. You can find the company ID on Myoperator Panel > Manage > Whatsapp APIs> company id

Phone number id: A unique identifier of Whatsapp phone number in MyOperator. You can find the ID by "List Phone numbers" or Go to Myoperator Panel > Manage > WhatsApp >WhatsApp Accounts >Phone number id

Waba id: A unique identifier of Whatsapp account. You can find the waba ID on Myoperator Panel > Manage > WhatsApp >Whatsapp Accounts >WABA ID

Template Variables: Template variables are used to send the template with variable. You can find the template variables in list template API or in Myoperator panel→ Manage→ WhatsApp→ Templates, hover on the variable to see the template variable name.

Media ID: Media ID is used to send the media(image/video/document) template You can use the "upload media" API which will return the media ID.

Errors and Status Codes

Standard HTTP error codes are returned in the case of a failure. 2xx codes indicate a successful message; 4xx codes indicate an error caused by information provided by the client; and 5xx codes indicate an error on MyOperator servers.

Status Codes

Status Code Meaning
200 OK
201 Created
400 Bad Request
404 Not found
403 Forbidden
500 Internal Server Error

Error Codes

CHAT_4001 Insufficient balance
CHAT_0301 Waba not approved by Meta

CHAT_0303 Phone number is disabled by chat service
CHAT_0304 Phone number not onboarded yet

CHAT_0004 Service inactive

item.description:
Webhooks are server callbacks from MyOperator's server to your own, triggered by specific events related to messages. These event-based notifications allow you to stay updated on message statuses.

To configure a webhook, go to MyOperator > Manage > API Integration > WhatsApp Webhook and set it up.

MyOperator sends the following payloads for message events:
Message Sent: Triggered when any message or template is sent via Live Chat, Campaign, or API.
Message Delivered: Triggered when a message or template is delivered to the customer.
Message Read: Triggered when a message or template is read by the customer.
Message Failed: Triggered when a message or template fails to send.

attribute name details
type This will contact set to "message"
source source from which message was initiated
lc - livechat
cmp - campaign
api - Public API
mode default set to "lc"
event This will provide the message status , following are the possible values

"sent" , "delivered" , "read" , "failed"
timestamp event timestamp
data.id unique message identifier which is used to send reply message
data.message_by Agent ID who send the message
data.action this denotes the whether message is incoming or outgoing
data.status same as event
data.is_reply if its a reply of another message
data.reply_to parent message id
data.metadata.waba_msg_id This is the waba message id
data.metadata.myop_ref_id User defined unique identifier
data.metadata.errors These are error codes

format will be
{ "WABA_meta_error_code": "" }
eg: {"WABA_131053": "Media upload error"}

for more information refer to the following documentation
https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/support/error-codes/
data.star_mark this is set to false by default for future enhancements
data.is_read is the event is "read" then this field is set to "true"
else its false
conversation.id this is unique conversation generated for the message sent.
conversation.customer_country_code Recipient country code
conversation.customer_contact Recipient Phone Number
conversation.customer_name Recipient name
conversation.assigned_to AgentID to which the conversation is assigned to
conversation.status conversation assigned status:
possible values for the following:

unassigned , assigned, closed
conversation.expire_at conversation expiry date . conversation expires 24 hours after last incoming message of the customer
conversation.last_message_at last message received or sent timestamp
conversation.created conversation created timestamp
conversation.modified conversation modified timestamp
conversation.unread_count conversation unread message count

request.description:
This API allows you to filter contacts dynamically using a flexible JSON-based query structure. You can apply filters on both standard fields and custom fields using supported operations.

🔹 Filter Structure

All filters must follow this structure:

{
    "and": {
        "<field_name>__<operation>": <value>
    }
}

  • and: Combines multiple conditions (logical AND)

  • : The field you want to filter on

  • : The operation to apply

  • : The value to compare against

✅ Standard Fields

  • name

  • country_code

  • phone_number_with_cc

  • email_id

  • marketing_opt_in

  • status

  • source

  • created

  • modified

🔸 Custom Fields

Custom fields must be referenced using the following format:

custom_fields.<field_id>

📌 Example:

custom_fields.my_custom_field_id_1

📎 To get your field_id, refer to:
👉 https://in.app.myoperator.com/contacts/custom-fields

🔹 Supported Operations

Operation Description Supported Data Types
is Equal to text, single_select, multi_select, switch, date, number
is_not Not equal to text, single_select, multi_select, date, number
contains Partial match (wildcard search) text, single_select, multi_select, text_area
not_contains Does not contain text, single_select, multi_select, text_area
is_set Field is not null or blank all types
is_not_set Field is null, blank, or does not exist all types
gt Greater than number, date
gte Greater than or equal to number, date
lt Less than number, date
lte Less than or equal to number, date
range Between two values (inclusive) date
not_range Not within a range date

🔹 Example Request

{
    "and":{
        "name__is": "John",
        "country_code__is": "91",
        "phone_number__is": "9876543210",
        "phone_number_with_cc__is": "919876543210",
        "email_id__contains": "john",
        "email_id__not_contains": "doe",
        "marketing_opt_in__is": true,
        "status__is_not": 0,
        "source__is": "manual_entry",
        "created__gt": "2025-01-01",
        "modified__lte": "2025-01-01",
        "custom_fields.my_custom_field_id_1__is": "prime", // customer_type (single_select type custom field with possible values: prime, regular)
        "custom_fields.my_custom_field_id_2__gte": 18, // age (number type custom field)
        "custom_fields.my_custom_field_id_3__range": {
            "gte": "1990-01-01",
            "lte": "1995-12-31",
        }, // dob (date type custom field)
        "custom_fields.my_custom_field_id_4__is": ["python", "php"], // skills (multi_select type custom field with possible values: python, php, mysql)
    }
}

🔹 Notes & Best Practices

  • Multiple filters inside "and" are combined using logical AND

  • Use correct data types for each operation (e.g., dates in YYYY-MM-DD)

  • multi_select fields accept arrays (e.g., ["python", "golang"])

  • range and not_range require both gte and lte

  • Always verify custom field IDs before use

This section contains all APIs related to managing contacts.

Body Parameters

The request body should be a JSON object containing the contact's details.

Parameter Type Required Description
name String Yes Full name of the contact.
country_code String Yes The contact's country code (e.g., "91").
phone_number String Yes The contact's phone number (e.g., "8449385515").
email_id String No The contact's email address.
marketing_opt_in Boolean No Set to true if the user has opted into marketing.
custom_fields Object No An object containing custom field data. See details below.

The custom_fields Object

This object allows you to save data to the custom fields you have defined in your MyOperator panel.

How to find Custom Field IDs

The "key" for each item in the custom_fields object must be the Custom Field ID.

To find this ID:

  1. Login to your MyOperator panel.

  2. Navigate to Contacts -> Custom Fields.

  3. Click Edit Custom Fields.

  4. Copy the value from the ID column. This value is the parameter name (key) you must use in the JSON payload.

Example Payload

Here is a full example of a request body that includes various types of custom fields.

{
  "name": "John Snow",
  "country_code": "91",
  "phone_number": "8449385515",
  "email_id": "user@example.com",
  "marketing_opt_in": true,
  "custom_fields": {
    "location": "Himachal pardesh",
    "address": "Himachal pardesh, dadh, 123456, palampur",
    "number": "1234567890",
    "gender": "male",

      "mysql"
    ],
    "dob": "1992-04-06",
    "appointment_time": "2025-02-02 20:11:11",

Note on Custom Field Types:
As shown in the example, the custom_fields object can support different data types as values:

  • String: "location": "Himachal pardesh"

  • Date: "dob": "1992-04-06"

  • Boolean: "local_user": false

item.description:
Webhooks are HTTP callbacks that receive notification messages for events. MyOperator uses webhooks to notify your application anytime a call or a message event happens in your account.

For example, if your agent has received a call,

  • You will receive a webhook during the call (in-call webhook).

  • After the call has finished (after-call webhook)

  • After any disposition has been submitted (disposition webhook).

Similarly, MyOperator sends the following payloads for message events:

  • Message Sent: Triggered when any message or template is sent via Live Chat, Campaign, or API.

  • Message Delivered: Triggered when a message or template is delivered to the customer.

  • Message Read: Triggered when the customer reads a message or template.

  • Message Failed: Triggered when a message or template fails to send.

Method

Webhooks are delivered using the HTTP POST method.

Whenever a configured event occurs (such as call events or message events), MyOperator sends an HTTP POST request to your configured Target URL. The request body contains the event payload in JSON format.

Content-Type Support:

The webhook event payload format depends on the Content-Type header configured for the webhook. The following content types are supported:

  • application/json

  • application/x-www-form-urlencoded

  • multipart/form-data

How data is sent for each Content-Type:

  1. application/json The complete event payload is sent as a JSON body.

  2. application/x-www-form-urlencoded The event payload fields are sent as form-encoded key-value pairs in the request body. Nested objects will be serialised appropriately within the form body.

  3. multipart/form-data The event payload fields are sent as multipart form fields in the request body.

If no Content-Type is explicitly configured, the webhook event will be sent with the default Content-Type: application/json.

Your webhook listener should:

  • Accept HTTP POST requests

  • Read and parse the request body based on the received Content-Type header

  • Return a 2xx status code to acknowledge successful receipt of the webhook

Headers

Headers are configured as key-value pairs in the panel. Any headers configured here will be included in the HTTP request when MyOperator sends the webhook to your Target URL.

This can be used for:

  • Authenticating incoming webhook requests

  • Passing secret tokens

  • Identifying the source of the request

  • Applying custom routing or validation logic at your server

For example, you can configure a header like:

  • Key: X-Webhook-Token

  • Value: your-secret-token

When the webhook is delivered, MyOperator will include this header in the request. Your server can then verify the header value to ensure that the request is coming from a trusted source.

Notes:

  • Multiple headers can be added as key-value pairs.

  • Header keys should follow standard HTTP header naming conventions.

  • Configured headers are appended to every webhook request regardless of the selected Content-Type.

Authentication

This component allows you to configure authentication for your webhook endpoint.

If your webhook listener is protected and requires authentication, you can provide the necessary credentials in this section. MyOperator will automatically include the configured authentication details when sending webhook requests.

Supported authentication types:

  1. No Auth
    No authentication headers will be added. The webhook will be sent as a standard HTTP POST request without any credentials.

  2. Basic Auth
    Use this option if your endpoint is protected using HTTP Basic Authentication.
    You can configure a username and password, and MyOperator will send the request with the appropriate Authorization: Basic header.

    Example configuration:

     {
  "username": "admin",
  "password": "123456"
 }

  3. API Key Auth
    Use this option if your endpoint requires an API key for authentication.
    The API key will be sent as a header in the webhook request using the configured key and value.

    Example configuration:

    • Key: X-API-Key

    • Value: your-api-key

Notes:

  • Authentication is applied to every webhook request once configured.

  • Ensure your endpoint can validate the selected authentication method.

  • If an authentication method (Basic Auth or API Key Auth) is enabled, it will override any conflicting headers configured in the Headers section.

  • Custom headers will still be included, except in cases where they conflict with auth-related headers (e.g., Authorisation).

Call Log

The call log payload is included in the After-call webhook and Disposition webhook events. These webhooks are triggered after a call has ended or when a disposition is submitted by the agent.

The call log contains detailed metadata about the call, such as caller information, timestamps, call status, agent details, recording information, and internal identifiers.

A call log is a hashmap (key-value pair) composed of several short field names with their values related to a call. The call log is provided in JSON format.

To reduce payload size and bandwidth usage, the field names are intentionally kept short. Because of this, it may not always be immediately clear what each field represents. The table below describes each field along with its meaning and example values.

Log Field name Description Example

_ai Call log id (unique for each call) abcdef123

The OBD Call API allows clients to initiate outbound calls through configured IVR routing.

Calls can be triggered using different dialer strategies depending on business workflow requirements.

Dialer Types

Type Dialer Mode Description
1 User Dialer Connects a call to a specific user/agent
1 Anonymous Dialer Bridges two external numbers
2 IVR Dialer Connects the customer directly to the IVR flow

Type = 3 dialer is deprecated and no longer supported.

Authentication

All requests must include an API Gateway token.

Header:

Header Required
x-api-key Yes

  • Values above limit → request rejected

  • Non-integer values → schema validation failure

The region filter will currently work as expected. In the future, however, it will be deprecated — you can use std_code instead.

Failover Routing Behaviour (Deprecated)

The failover campaign setting has been deprecated.

Calls are now routed by default using the DIDs mapped directly to the campaign configuration.

No additional fallback campaign configuration is required.

If calls must be initiated from a single specific DID, ensure that only that DID is mapped to the campaign.

API Gateway Validation

Occurs when the request does not match the schema.

Examples:

  • Missing required field

  • Incorrect datatype

  • Invalid JSON structure

Response format may differ from application responses.

Application Validation

Occurs when a request is structurally valid but fails business rules.

Examples:

  • Unauthorised source IP

  • Billing or usage expiry

  • Routing configuration not available

  • Dialer type rule violations

  • Threshold limits exceeded

Response Behaviour

200 — Request Accepted

Returned when the request is successfully queued for processing.

A warning acceptance may be returned when routing resources are not guaranteed (e.g., call_hold disabled).

400 — Bad Request

Returned for invalid request parameters, including:

  • Invalid number format

  • max_call_duration violations

403 — Forbidden

Returned when the request is not permitted due to:

  • Usage threshold exceeded

  • Billing expiry

  • Invalid field usage for selected dialer type

404 — Not Found

Returned when requested, IVR or routing configuration is not available.

500 — Internal Server Error

The call.dial_begin event represents the stage where the system starts dialing a participant (agent or customer).

This event provides detailed information about the dialing process through the legs array.

Event Structure

This webhook follows the standard envelope + payload structure:

  • Root fields contain event metadata (routing, identification, sequencing)

  • payload contains call routing and participant details

Payload Overview

  • The payload contains a legs array describing participants involved in dialing

  • If no second party is involved (e.g., IVR-only flow or missed call), this event may not be triggered

  • The legs array may be empty in case of missed calls or misdials

Call Type → Leg Mapping

  • Incoming call → leg1 = customer, leg2 = agent

  • Oneway call → leg1 = agent, leg2 = customer

  • Callback call → leg1 = agent/customer, leg2 = customer/agent

  • Webcall outgoing → leg1 = agent, leg2 = customer

  • OBD (agent first) → leg1 = agent, leg2 = customer

  • OBD (customer first) → leg1 = customer, leg2 = agent

  • OTP call → No event generated

Payload Schema

Top-Level

Field Type Description
legs array Array representing the participants involved in dialing

Leg Object Schema

Field Type Description
leg_index int Monotonically increasing index (starts from 1)
type string agent or customer
phone_number string E.164 formatted phone number
pickup_device string phone or web
dept_id string Department ID initiating the dial (empty if not applicable)
started_at time Dial start time (millisecond precision, NEVER blank)
answered_at time Time when call was answered (null if not answered)
ended_at time Time when call ended (null until hangup)
result string Current state: answered, not_answered, dialing, connected
ring_duration int Ringing duration (answered_at - started_at). Null for incoming leg
talk_duration int Talk duration. Null if not answered
dial_status string Operator status: ANSWER, NO ANSWER, BUSY, NO CARRIER, CANCEL (blank for incoming leg)

The call.answered event is triggered when a participant (agent or customer) answers the call.

This event provides details about the participant who answered, along with the current state of all call legs.

Event Structure

This webhook follows the standard envelope + payload structure:

  • Root fields contain event metadata (routing, identification, sequencing)

  • payload contains call participant details

Payload Overview

The payload contains a legs array representing all participants involved in the call.

  • The leg with result = answered indicates the participant who just answered

  • Other legs represent the current state of the call

answered_at time Time when call was answered
ended_at time Time when call ended (null until hangup)
result string Current state (answered, connected, etc.)

The call.end event represents the final state of a call.

It contains the complete call summary, including all historical data related to the call and every leg involved. This is the final event for a call session.

Event Structure

This webhook follows the standard envelope + payload structure:

  • Root fields contain event metadata

  • payload contains the complete call summary

Payload Overview

The payload object for call.end contains:

  • All top-level call fields

  • Complete legs array with final state of all participants

Payload Schema

Field Type Description
id string The UID assigned by the system for this call
category string incoming, oneway, callback, webcall, obd, otp
direction string incoming or outgoing
status string bridged, missed, voicemail
started_at time Call start time (never blank)
ended_at time Call end time
duration int Total duration of the call (seconds)
billable bool True if billable
ref_id string System-generated reference ID for OBD calls
client_ref_id string Client-provided reference ID for OBD calls
obd_campaign object OBD campaign details (only for OBD calls)
obd_campaign.job_id string Campaign job ID
obd_campaign.id string Campaign IVR ID
recording_filename string Recording file name
legs array Final state of all call participants

call.summary

The call.summary event is the final event in the call lifecycle.

It contains the complete and enriched call log, including:

  • Final call details

  • All participants (legs)

  • Agent and department metadata

  • Comments added during the call

This is the most comprehensive event for a session and should be used for:

  • CRM updates

  • Analytics

  • Reporting

  • Final state processing

Event Structure

This webhook follows the standard envelope + payload structure:

  • Root fields contain event metadata

  • payload contains the complete call summary

Payload Overview

The payload object contains:

  • All top-level call fields

  • Full legs array (never empty)

  • comments array (if any comments were added)

  • Additional metadata such as agent and department details

Payload Schema

Field Type Description
id string The UID assigned by the system for this call
category string incoming, oneway, callback, webcall, obd, otp
direction string incoming or outgoing
location string Customer location in format “State, Country” (may be empty or approximate)
customer_number string Customer phone number (10-digit format)
status string bridged, missed, voicemail
started_at time Call start time (never blank)
ended_at time Call end time
duration int Total call duration (seconds)
billable bool True if billable
ref_id string System-generated reference ID (OBD only)
client_ref_id string Client-provided reference ID (OBD only)
obd_campaign object OBD campaign details (if applicable)
obd_campaign.job_id string Campaign job ID
obd_campaign.id string Campaign IVR ID
recording_filename string Recording file name
legs array Call participants (never empty)
comments array Comments added during the call

Legs Object (Additional Fields)

In addition to fields present in call.end, each leg includes:

Field Type Description
agent object Agent details (if applicable)
department object Department associated with the leg

User Object (agent / posted_by)

Field Type Description
uuid string Unique user ID
name string User name
email string User email
extension string User extension
contact string User phone number

Department Object

Field Type Description
id string Department ID
name string Department name

Comments Object

Field Type Description
id string Comment ID
content string Comment text
posted_at time Timestamp when comment was added
posted_by object User who posted the comment

Disposition Webhook

The Disposition Webhook enables clients to perform actions based on the disposition data added to a call.

This webhook is triggered when a disposition is submitted for a call and can be used to:

  • Collect call and disposition data in your datastore

  • Trigger custom integrations (e.g., create/update leads in CRM)

Event Overview

  • This is a single event (not lifecycle-based)

  • Triggered after a disposition is submitted

  • Contains:

    • Disposition data

    • Comments (if added)

Payload Overview

The payload contains:

  • dispositions array (at least one entry)

  • comments array (can be empty)

Payload Schema

Dispositions

Field Type Description
dispositions[].type int Type of Disposition: 1 or 2
dispositions[].name string Disposition name
dispositions[].user_id string User ID who submitted disposition
dispositions[].added_at time Timestamp when disposition was added

Comments

Field Type Description
comments[].id string Comment ID
comments[].content string Comment text
comments[].posted_at time Timestamp when comment was added
comments[].posted_by object User who added the comment

Comment Author (posted_by)

Field Type Description
uuid string User ID
name string User name
email string Email of user. Returns empty string ("") if not available
extension int User extension. Returned as integer in actual payload
contact string Phone number with country code

Calls Webhooks Overview

Call webhooks allow you to track the complete lifecycle of a voice call in real time — from initiation to completion.

By listening to different event_type values, you can reconstruct the full journey of a call and build logic for CRM updates, analytics, or automation workflows.

Event Lifecycle

An Event Lifecycle represents the complete set of events generated during a session.

  • All events are grouped using a common session_id and channel

  • For simple or historical events (e.g., disposition), only a single event may be sent

  • For calls, multiple events together form a full lifecycle

By tracking event_type, you can follow a session from start to finish.

Call Event Lifecycle

A typical call goes through multiple stages:

  1. Call is initiated

  2. System dials the target (agent/extension)

  3. Call is answered

  4. Call ends and summary is generated

Events in Order

  • call.initiated
    Call session is created

  • call.ivr_started
    Call reaches IVR (if applicable)

  • call.dial_begin
    System starts dialing a target

  • call.answered
    Call is answered

  • call.end
    Final event after hangup
    Includes durations, analytics, and recording details

  • call.summary
    Final comprehensive summary of the entire call session
    Contains the complete call log and structured overview

Understanding Call Transfers

Call transfers are handled using the same event structure (no separate transfer event).

  • Each transfer creates a new call.dial_begin event

  • The leg_index increments with each transfer

Example:

  • Agent A answers → leg_index = 1

  • Call transferred to Agent B → new dial event with leg_index = 2

This creates a clean, sequential timeline of the call.

Key Takeaways

  • Use event_type to track call progression

  • Use event_sequence (from root) to maintain order

  • Use customer_identifier for CRM mapping

item.description:
MyOperator sends the following payloads for message events:

  • message.sent: Triggered when any message or template is sent via Live Chat, Campaign, or API.

  • message.received: Triggered when any message is received.

  • message.delivered: Triggered when a message or template is delivered to the customer.

  • message.read: Triggered when the customer reads a message or template.

  • message.failed: Triggered when a message or template fails to send.

  • message.link_tracking: Triggered when the template Track URL is clicked.

  • conversation.assign: Triggered when a conversation is assigned

  • conversation.close: Triggered when a conversation is closed.

Webhooks Overview

Webhooks are HTTP callbacks that receive event notifications. MyOperator uses webhooks to notify your application whenever a call or message event occurs in your account.

Whether you are building a CRM integration, analytics pipeline, or internal dashboard, webhooks provide real-time, event-driven updates for all communication activities.

For example, if your agent has received a call:

  • You will receive a webhook during the call (in-call webhook)

  • After the call has finished (after-call webhook)

  • After any disposition has been submitted (disposition webhook)

Similarly, MyOperator sends the following payloads for message events:

  • Message Sent: Triggered when any message or template is sent via Live Chat, Campaign, or API

  • Message Delivered: Triggered when a message or template is delivered to the customer

  • Message Read: Triggered when the customer reads a message or template

  • Message Failed: Triggered when a message or template fails to send

Webhook Event Structure (Envelope Model)

All webhook payloads follow a flattened envelope structure.

  • The root level (envelope) contains static metadata used for routing and identification

  • The payload object contains event-specific data

This design ensures faster processing and avoids deeply nested JSON structures.

Root Fields

Field Type Description
event_id string Unique identifier of the event (used for deduplication)
company_id string Unique identifier of your MyOperator account
event_type string Type of event (e.g., call.answered, message.sent)
event_sequence integer Sequence of events within a session (1, 2, 3...)
event_version integer Version of the event schema
timestamp datetime Event timestamp in ISO 8601 format
channel string Communication channel (call, WhatsApp)
direction string incoming/outgoing (can be empty for non-directional events)
session_id string Unique session identifier (call ID or conversation ID)
system_identifier string Your system number (DID, Caller ID, or WhatsApp number)
customer_identifier string Customer phone number (remains constant per session)
payload object Event-specific details

Delivery Method

Webhooks are delivered using the HTTP POST method.

Whenever a configured event occurs (such as call events or message events), MyOperator sends an HTTP POST request to your configured Target URL. The request body contains the event payload.

Content-Type Support

The webhook event payload format depends on the Content-Type header configured for the webhook.

Supported Content Types

  • application/json

  • application/x-www-form-urlencoded

  • multipart/form-data

Payload Behavior

  • application/json
    The complete event payload is sent as a JSON body

  • application/x-www-form-urlencoded
    The payload is sent as key-value pairs (nested objects are serialised appropriately)

  • multipart/form-data
    The payload is sent as multipart form fields

If no Content-Type is configured, the default is application/json.

Webhook Listener Requirements

Your webhook endpoint should:

  • Accept HTTP POST requests

  • Parse the request body based on Content-Type

  • Return a 2xx status code to acknowledge successful receipt

Integration Best Practices

To ensure reliable webhook processing, follow these guidelines:

  1. Respond Quickly
    Always return HTTP 200 OK immediately after receiving the webhook.
    If processing is heavy, queue the event and process it asynchronously.

  2. Idempotency (event_id)
    Webhook retries may occur due to network issues.
    Use event_id to detect duplicates and avoid reprocessing the same event.

  3. Event Ordering (event_sequence)
    Events may arrive out of order.
    Use event_sequence to process events in the correct chronological order.

  4. Phone Number Format (E.164)
    All phone numbers (system_identifier, customer_identifier) follow E.164 format.

Example: +919876543210

Use this format for consistent lookups in your system.

Headers

Headers are configured as key-value pairs in the panel. These headers are included in every webhook request.

Use Cases

  • Authentication

  • Passing secret tokens

  • Identifying the request source

  • Custom validation logic

Example

Key: X-Webhook-Token Value: your-secret-token

Notes

  • Multiple headers can be added

  • Headers are included in all webhook requests

  • Follow standard HTTP header naming conventions

Authentication

You can configure authentication for webhook delivery.

Supported Types

No Auth
No authentication headers are added.

  • Basic Auth
    Uses HTTP Basic Authentication.

    • Example:
      { "username": "admin", "password": "123456" }

  • API Key Auth
    Sends API key as a header.

    • Example:
      Key: X-API-Key Value: your-api-key

Important Notes

  • Authentication applies to all webhook requests once configured

  • Authentication overrides conflicting headers (e.g., Authorisation)

  • Custom headers are still included unless they conflict with auth headers

request.description:
Overview

The Search Logs API allows you to retrieve call activity logs from your MyOperator account using flexible search and filtering options.

This API supports querying logs using date ranges, keyword search, pagination, and filters, enabling developers to retrieve specific call records efficiently.

Filters allow advanced querying of logs and are constructed using filter identifiers retrieved from the Log Filters API.

Setting Up Filters

To use filters in the Search Logs API, follow the steps below:

Step 1 — Fetch Available Filters

Call the Log Filters API to retrieve the list of available filters.

Each filter returned by this API includes a filter ID that corresponds to a specific log attribute.

These filter IDs can be used to construct filter queries for the Search Logs API.

Step 2 — Build Filter Conditions

Using the filter IDs retrieved in Step 1, construct filter conditions by combining them with logical operators.

Supported logical operators include:

  • AND

  • OR

Parentheses can be used to define logical grouping.

Step 3 — Add Filters to the Search Request

Pass the constructed filter expression in the filters parameter of the Search Logs API request.

Example filter expression:

12 AND (5 OR 8)

In this example:

  • 12, 5, and 8 are filter IDs retrieved from the Log Filters API

  • AND and OR define how the conditions are combined

Request Body Parameters

Parameter Type Description
token string Public API token used to authenticate the request.
from integer Start timestamp (UTC Unix time) from which logs should be retrieved.
to integer End timestamp (UTC Unix time) for the logs query.
log_from integer Offset used for pagination when retrieving logs.
page_size integer Number of logs returned in a single request (default: 20, maximum: 100).
search_key string Keyword used to search logs across fields such as caller name, phone number, email, and comments.
filters string Logical expression built using filter IDs retrieved from the Log Filters API.

Pagination

The API supports pagination to retrieve large volumes of logs efficiently.

Parameter Description
log_from Offset used to fetch logs from a specific position.
page_size Number of records returned in a single request.

Use the value returned in the previous response to fetch the next set of logs.

Notes

  • A valid Public API token must be included in every request.

  • The Log Filters API must be called first to obtain filter IDs.

  • Filters can be combined using logical operators such as AND and OR.

  • Pagination parameters should be used when retrieving large datasets.

Overview

The Log Filters API allows you to retrieve a list of available filters that can be used to refine and customise queries in the Search Logs API. Each filter represents a specific attribute of call logs (such as call type, status, source, etc.) and is associated with a unique filter ID. These filter IDs are required to construct logical filter expressions when querying logs using the Search Logs API.

Purpose of Log Filters

The Log Filters API is used to discover all available filters supported by the system, retrieve the filter IDs required to build filter expressions, and understand the possible filtering options for call log queries.

How It Works

  1. Call the Log Filters API

  2. Retrieve the list of filters along with their corresponding IDs

  3. Use these IDs to construct logical expressions

  4. Pass the constructed expression in the filters parameter of the Search Logs API

Response Structure

The API returns a flat list of filters. Each filter contains:

  • id → Unique identifier for the filter

  • name → Human-readable name of the filter

  • parent_id → Indicates hierarchy (0 = parent filter, non-zero = child filter)

Parent-child relationships help group filters logically.

Example Response

{
    "status": "success",
    "code": 200,
    "filters": [
        {
            "id": "1",
            "name": "Source of logs",
            "parent_id": "0"
        },
        {
            "id": "2",
            "name": "Myoperator IVR",
            "parent_id": "1"
        },
        {
            "id": "3",
            "name": "Mobile",
            "parent_id": "1"
        },
        {
            "id": "4",
            "name": "Event of logs",
            "parent_id": "0"
        }
    ]
}

Understanding Filter Hierarchy

  • Filters with parent_id = 0 are root categories

  • Filters with non-zero parent_id are child filters under a category

Example:

  • Source of logs (id: 1) is a parent filter

    • Myoperator IVR (id: 2)

    • Mobile (id: 3)

Using Filters in Search Logs API

Each filter has a unique id which is used to build logical expressions, i.e., ' 2 OR 3`

  • 2 and 3 are filter IDs under the same parent

  • OR is used to match any condition

You can also combine filters across categories, i.e:- 2 AND 4

Notes

  • The Log Filters API must be called before using filters in the Search Logs API

  • Filter IDs are dynamic and may change based on account configuration

  • Always fetch the latest filters before constructing queries

  • Supported logical operators: AND, OR

  • Parentheses can be used for grouping conditions
